summary.headline: CreditAccess Grameen Q1 FY27 PAT rose 720% YoY to INR 493 Crore, ROA 5.9%, ROE 24.4%, with AUM up 16.4% YoY to INR 30,319 Crore.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of the strongest first quarters in company history, with AUM growth of 16.4% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, PPOP up 33.6% YoY to INR 873 Crore, and gross NPA falling to 2.18%. Credit cost was INR 212 Crore (0.72% non-annualised, roughly 2.8-2.9% annualised) against a 3-4% full-year guidance. Retail finance rose to 20.6% of AUM, and management reiterated the INR 50,000 Crore AUM target for calendar 2028 but kept FY27 guidance unchanged pending one more quarter. Management flagged a possible 50 bps MFI pricing cut from Q3 and another 50 bps in Q4, conditional on credit cost.

financial_highlights.change: Approx. 2.8-2.9% annualised per analyst calculation, not disputed by management
Improving yields and lower interest reversals
From INR 2,734 Crore in FY20, 20% CAGR; 86% from internal accruals
10-15 bps impact from longer-tenor ECB/NCD mix shift

segments.name: Microfinance (group lending)
segments.commentary: Unique group lending borrowers are 45.7% of AUM; borrowers with more than 3 lenders are 2.6% of AUM. Management expects about 1 lakh new borrowers per month going forward, and 2.5 lakh were added in Q1 (35% new-to-credit).

segments.name: Retail finance
segments.commentary: Now 20.6% of AUM, up from 18.1% in Q4 FY26. Unnati is 100% internal sourcing with average vintage of 7.7 years and average credit score of 732; its PAR 30 never exceeded about 3% in the prior cycle. Mortgage is about INR 270 Crore, with 55% internal and 45% external sourcing, and is about 1% of AUM.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: Described as the one product not yet profitable, though it is a small book. Sourced through the company's own branches and customers, with dealers used for fulfilment only.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged for now; management will observe one more quarter before revisiting. Management said it sees nothing on the ground that would require a change.
Medium-term AUM target of INR 50,000 Crore by calendar year 2028, with no fundraise needed (funded from internal accruals).
Full-year credit cost guidance of 3-4%; management said it may land at the lower end if no upside risks emerge.

Pricing: management said a 50 bps MFI price cut is possible by end-Q2 FY27 if asset quality holds. Nilesh Dalvi said the cut may come in Q3 and another 50 bps in Q4, gradually and linked to credit cost. Benefit passed on in H2 FY27 per board pricing policy.
Cross-cycle target restated as ROA about 4.5% and ROE about 18-20%. Management said it would not cap ROA during the up-cycle and expects FY27 ROA well above the 4-5% range if Q1 trends hold.
Stage 1 provisioning expected to stay at about 1.63% through Q2 unless West Asia-related fuel shortages or other external events raise the ECL overlay.
capex_capacity: Network at 2,276 branches across 457 districts after 42 new branches in Q1 (+7.7% YoY).
Employees at 21,981 (+3% YoY); attrition 20.6% vs 25.8% a year earlier.
Branch and headcount expansion is already budgeted in the plan; management said no extra funding is needed.
Grameen Mahi app: 4 lakh onboarded in Q1, 15.4 lakh active customers (34.5% of borrowers). Digital collections at 24.2% of total, up from 16.3% in FY26.
Undrawn funding lines of INR 2,993 Crore and a funding pipeline of INR 9,440 Crore.
demand_pricing: Credit cost: trailing 12-month credit cost is about 4.0-4.5%, which Nilesh Dalvi said is why the current 14% NIM is elevated. Management expects trailing credit cost to fall toward about 3% if the current trend holds.
Collections: X-bucket collection efficiency 99.68% for June 2026. Average PAR 15 accretion around 15 bps per month in Q1 (about 15-20 bps over the first four months).
Write-offs: Q1 write-offs relate to stress from Q2 FY26; management expects normative write-offs from Q2 onwards, which should lower credit cost.

Pricing: retail lending rates are about 50 bps above MFI for unsecured business loans and about 1% below MFI for loans against property (around 20.5%). Over 99% of AUM is at 20%+ yields, per Nilesh Dalvi.
Yield rose about 60 bps QoQ, partly from lower interest reversals; management said yield should settle at current levels until any customer price cut.

qa_highlights.question: Does El Nino or the West Asia war risk current momentum, and would guidance change in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Narayanan said nothing visible on the ground and no leading indicators of stress; guidance kept as is for one more quarter. Management reported no discernible West Asia impact so far.

qa_highlights.question: How long before non-MFI products drag on P&L, and when will they reach steady-state returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most products are already profitable, including mortgage before HO allocation; only two-wheeler is not yet profitable. Mortgage needs about INR 1,000 Crore to reach full breakeven including HO allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How should the 14% NIM and 24% ROE be read against the full-year guidance, and how much pricing cut is coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may cut 50 bps in Q3 and another 50 bps in Q4, not 200-250 bps, and only if credit cost trends hold. Assets take 15-18 months to reprice. Nilesh Dalvi said NIM would be about 13-13.5% if credit cost settles near 3%, supporting about 4.5% ROA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-4% credit cost guidance conservative, and what PAR accretion is built in?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Dalvi said the range is a cushion for West Asia and monsoon risk; if no upside risks appear, the company may end at the lower end. He did not give a specific PAR accretion assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Stage 1 provisioning: will it rise toward 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Narayanan said Stage 1 PCR is 1.63%, unchanged this quarter, and an ECL committee now reviews it quarterly. It could rise if fuel shortages from the West Asia crisis develop; otherwise it is expected to stay in range.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA stay above the 4-5% range in the up-cycle, and will there be overlay provisions or spending?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Dalvi said the company will not cap ROA and expects FY27 ROA well above 4-5% if Q1 trends continue. Management said there is an INR 41 Crore West Asia overlay, that more could follow in Q2 depending on weather, and that expansion is already budgeted.

risks_watch: Monsoon and El Nino effects on rural cash flows; management will watch the next 2-3 months.
West Asia crisis: possible fuel shortages could raise the Stage 1 ECL overlay (INR 41 Crore overlay already booked).
Trailing credit cost (about 4.0-4.5%) must drop toward 3% for the planned 50 bps cuts in Q3 and Q4.
Retail mortgage book is small (about INR 270 Crore), so credit cost in this segment may be lumpy as it scales.
Customer KYC gaps (voter ID is the main ID in MFI); management said the impact is not significant but could not quantify it.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 results and the asset quality trend, but deliberately noncommittal on FY27 guidance, which it will revisit after one more quarter. Management was specific on pricing (50 bps steps, linked to credit cost) and cautious about external risks (West Asia, El Nino).
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been one of our strongest Q1 in the history of the company, marked by robust portfolio growth, normalized asset quality, and profitability levels that reflect the underlying strength and resilience of our franchise.
It is purely linked to how the credit cost trend is shaping up.
There's absolutely nothing on the ground. There are also no leading indicators indicate any buildup of additional stress at this point.

growth.why: FY27 guidance held unchanged pending one more quarter, with AUM target of INR 50,000 Cr by CY2028 reiterated; growth backed by 42 new branches, 2.5 lakh new borrowers in Q1, and undrawn lines of INR 2,993 Cr plus a INR 9,440 Cr funding pipeline, but no specific FY27 revenue growth number was given.
